source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Nitrazine paper turns blue with vaginal fluid. What does this mean?
questions.rationale: Blue (alkaline) indicates amniotic fluid; red (acidic) indicates urine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nitrazine Test (PDF p. 200)
questions.quote: Blue (alkaline): Amniotic fluid

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman has a strong urge to push at 8 cm. What should the nurse tell her?
questions.rationale: Do not push before full dilation; pant-breathe with the urge to push.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Second Stage (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Ask client to pant-breathe if there is an urge to push

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which sequence correctly begins the cardinal movements of labor?
questions.rationale: Mechanisms of labor: engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, external rotation, expulsion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mechanisms of Labor (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Mechanisms of Labor (ED FIRE ERE)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Under EINC, when is the cord clamped?
questions.rationale: EINC: immediate drying, skin-to-skin, properly timed cord clamping (after pulsations stop or 1–3 minutes), and early breastfeeding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EINC (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Properly timed cord clamping (when pulsation stops or after 2 minutes)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which sign shows the placenta has separated?
questions.rationale: Signs: Calkin's sign (firm, globular uterus), cord lengthening, sudden gush of blood, uterus rising.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Calkin's Sign (Uterus becomes firm and globular)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: After how long is the third stage of labor considered prolonged?
questions.rationale: The third stage usually lasts 5–10 minutes; beyond 30 minutes is abnormal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Beyond 30 minutes is already abnormal

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A placenta delivers with the shiny fetal side first. This is:
questions.rationale: Schultze is shiny, separates from the center, with less bleeding; Duncan is raw and red with more bleeding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Placental Expulsion (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Shiny and glistening from the fetal membranes

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: How many vessels does a normal umbilical cord have?
questions.rationale: A normal cord has two arteries and one vein (AVA).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: 2 arteries and 1 vein (AVA)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: When is methylergonovine (Methergine) given?
questions.rationale: Ergot drugs cause strong contraction and can trap the placenta, so they are given after placental delivery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage Drugs (PDF p. 201)
questions.quote: Best given immediately after delivery of placenta

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Why is the fourth stage of labor most risky for a woman with heart disease?
questions.rationale: Retained fluid is reabsorbed, increasing cardiac output and oxygen demand.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fourth Stage (PDF p. 202)
questions.quote: most detrimental or difficult stage of labor in gravidocardiac patients

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A woman at 10 weeks has bleeding with a closed cervix. What type of abortion is this?
questions.rationale: Threatened abortion: bleeding without cervical dilation or effacement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Abortion (PDF p. 202)
questions.quote: Threatened Abortion Presence of vaginal bleeding; no cervical dilation and effacement

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What is the most common predisposing factor for ectopic pregnancy?
questions.rationale: PID is the most common predisposing factor; previous surgery, IUD, and prior ectopic also increase risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ectopic Pregnancy (PDF p. 202)
questions.quote: Most common predisposing factor: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Bluish discoloration around the umbilicus in ruptured ectopic pregnancy is:
questions.rationale: Cullen's sign is periumbilical ecchymosis from hemoperitoneum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ectopic Pregnancy (PDF p. 203)
questions.quote: Positive (+) for Cullen's Sign

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which drug may treat an unruptured ectopic pregnancy under 3 cm?
questions.rationale: Methotrexate, given IM, destroys fast-growing trophoblast cells in small ectopics.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ectopic Pregnancy (PDF p. 203)
questions.quote: Given I.M. to the mother if ectopic pregnancy is less than 3 cm

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which finding suggests hydatidiform mole?
questions.rationale: H-mole shows rapid uterine enlargement, hyperemesis from high hCG, pinkish discharge, and no FHT.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hydatidiform Mole (PDF p. 203)
questions.quote: Rapid abdominal enlargement

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After D&C for H-mole, what should the woman avoid for 1 year?
questions.rationale: hCG is monitored for a year to detect choriocarcinoma; pregnancy would confuse results.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hydatidiform Mole (PDF p. 203)
questions.quote: No pregnancy for 1 year

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of habitual abortion?
questions.rationale: Premature cervical dilation (incompetent cervix) is the most common cause of habitual abortion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Premature Cervical Dilation (PDF p. 204)
questions.quote: Most common cause of habitual abortion

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: When are McDonald cerclage sutures removed?
questions.rationale: McDonald sutures are removed at 37–38 weeks to allow vaginal delivery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Premature Cervical Dilation (PDF p. 204)
questions.quote: Sutures are removed 37 to 38 weeks of pregnancy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Painless, bright red bleeding at 34 weeks suggests:
questions.rationale: Placenta previa is the most common cause of painless third-trimester bleeding; abruption is painful.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Placenta Previa (PDF p. 204)
questions.quote: Most common cause of painless bleeding in the third trimester of pregnancy

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which action is CONTRAINDICATED with painless bleeding late in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Never do pelvic or rectal exams with suspected placenta previa; they can cause hemorrhage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Placenta Previa (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: Never attempt a pelvic or rectal examination with painless bleeding late in pregnancy

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Sharp fundal pain with a rigid, board-like uterus suggests:
questions.rationale: Abruption causes sharp stabbing pain, uterine rigidity, and bleeding that may be concealed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Abruptio Placenta (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: Rigidity of the uterus

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Blood seeping into the myometrium in central abruption causes:
questions.rationale: Couvelaire uterus is bluish, copper-colored, and atonic, often requiring hysterectomy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Abruptio Placenta (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: Couvelaire Uterus

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: The cord prolapses after membranes rupture. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Do not reinsert; cover with NSS-moistened gauze, give oxygen, and check FHT; prepare for delivery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PROM (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Moisten gauze with NSS and cover the cord

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which drug hastens fetal lung maturity in preterm rupture of membranes?
questions.rationale: Corticosteroids such as betamethasone hasten fetal lung maturity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PROM (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Corticosteroid such as Betamethasone to hasten fetal lung maturity

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Why is IV fluid given in preterm labor?
questions.rationale: Good hydration may stop contractions; bed rest and tocolytics are also used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Premature Labor (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: hydration may stop contractions

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: In the BUBBLE-HE postpartum check, 'H' stands for:
questions.rationale: Breasts, Uterus, Bladder, Bowels, Lochia, Episiotomy, Homans' sign, and Emotions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postpartum Assessment (PDF p. 202)
questions.quote: Homan’s sign: pain upon dorsiflexion (possible deep vein thrombosis)
